section: A Declared-Authority Architecture and Its Measured Cost
text: Report prepared 21 August – 8 September 2026.

section: Abstract
text: Home Assistant reports 669,743 active installations [1], and a third-party integration installed into one of them executes inside the platform's own process with the platform's own authority.

section: Abstract
text: There is no permission model, no scoping rule and no caller check [2]: an integration that declares itself a temperature sensor may call `lock.unlock`, read every stored credential, reach the home network, and — as Corno and Mannella demonstrate [9] — walk the Python garbage collector to another integration's live object and read its secrets.

section: Abstract
text: The 2021 disclosures show this is not hypothetical for this ecosystem [4][6].

section: Abstract
text: **This work designs, builds and evaluates confinement for these integrations without modifying them**, on the ground that the declaration such a scheme needs already exists in every integration's manifest and is currently spent on a log line and a discovery heuristic.

section: Abstract
text: Enforcement is placed outside the integration's process, because the garbage-collector result eliminates every in-process design; the integration runs unmodified inside Linux namespaces, seccomp and cgroup v2, against a real stripped Home Assistant, and reaches the platform and the network only through a mediator that holds the credential it never sees.

section: Abstract
text: **The cost of confinement, measured against an unconfined baseline on the same host and release, is zero at the import level.** Across 77 community integrations on two corpora sharing 5% of their members — 37 by install count and 40 drawn uniformly — the confined and unconfined arms fail on the *same* integrations for the *same* reasons: 84% and 92% clean in both arms, so the failures attributable to the design number none, twice.

section: Abstract
text: Ten integrations were executed end to end, a named set rather than a sample, the ceiling being that 26 of 37 need a credential before any configuration flow completes.

section: Abstract
text: All ten load confined, and the five that poll a remote API matched their unconfined output — exactly for three, and within the minute-to-minute movement of a live value for two — through mediated connections logged to a named host and port, over three different network stacks; one of them did so with a valid account credential that never reached the mediator.

section: Abstract
text: On the Raspberry Pi 5 the requirements name, mediation costs 31.5 µs and the audit record is durable before the action it records at 3.67 ms, 63× clear of realistic demand.

section: Abstract
text: Against the house's real Home Assistant, a confined integration's entities are registry entities with their unconfined names and survive a restart, real changes reach it within a millisecond, and a user's command reaches the integration's own code in 16 ms.

section: Abstract
text: A sandbox that floods the mediator with refused requests is stopped after 100 of them, within a second, and the household is told in Home Assistant's own Repairs panel and can restart it without widening what it may do.

section: Abstract
text: **The most useful result was a failure, and it arrived last.** Running a single real community integration confined against its own real API found that the platform's own HTTP helper could not be constructed inside the sandbox at all — `async_get_clientsession` builds its resolver by instantiating Zeroconf, which joins the multicast group, and a fresh network namespace's loopback carries no multicast flag.

section: Abstract
text: The egress design had therefore been unusable for the 41% of the corpus it exists to serve, for as long as it had existed, **behind eighteen suites that all passed**, because every earlier subject had been written by the author of the sandbox.

section: Abstract
text: Three more real integrations, chosen by network stack, then found three further defects of the same kind behind twenty passing suites — an instance missing two pieces a real startup provides, and a sandbox with no certificate authorities — and two of them had already produced wrong attributions, one through a paired baseline that shared the fault it was meant to control for.

section: Abstract
text: Building the push loop then found that the mediator had recorded each action *after* carrying it out, for every operation that acts, from the day acting was implemented until 2026-10-04: the ordering the audit log exists to guarantee had held only in the self-test that staged it by hand.

section: Abstract
text: Four other mechanisms in this project each caught a class of error — a paired baseline stopped three misattributions, two instruments bounded each other, a self-test passed when the surprising thing was true, a figure was recomputed from its source — and none of the four could have found this one, because all four are written out of the same assumptions as the thing they test.

section: Abstract
text: Six of eight predictions registered before measurement were wrong and none was revised.

section: Abstract
text: Until the last of those real integrations, every correction across eight chapters had been to a sentence next to a measurement rather than to a measurement, apart from defects found in the artifact itself — one by writing an attack, four by running real integrations, and three by wiring the durable audit log into every harness.

section: Abstract
text: Two of the four ended that record: an instance missing what a real startup provides had made one integration in five look like confinement's cost, and on a corrected instance the end-to-end cost is none.

section: 5.2 The design problem, restated precisely
text: From `hass`, the following are reachable by ordinary attribute access: the shared data dictionary holding every integration's runtime state, the event bus, the service registry, the state machine, the configuration directory path, the authentication manager, the HTTP server, every integration's stored configuration, and the event loop itself.

section: 5.2 The design problem, restated precisely
text: **The decisive property is that none of this is conferred by a grant that could be withheld.** Two facts establish it.

section: 5.2 The design problem, restated precisely
text: **First, no in-process control can be sound.** A permission layer living in the same interpreter as the code it constrains is an object in that interpreter's heap, reachable by the same technique.

section: 5.2 The design problem, restated precisely
text: This is why S2 requires that the confined code hold no such credential, and it is why this project is complementary to that proposal rather than competing with it: the proposal supplies a mechanism for moving code, and what is missing from it is the scoping.

section: 5.2 The design problem, restated precisely
text: **Third, the design target is now expressible in one sentence.** The confined integration must be somewhere that confers no authority, while still being able to obtain — by request, subject to a decision — exactly the authority its manifest declares.

section: 5.3 Where enforcement can live

section: 5.4 Decision 1 — the platform
text: The evidence that made it is: an ecosystem of 4,220 community integrations installed on 56.6% of reporting installations (§1.3); a documented incident class in this specific ecosystem, the 2021 disclosures affecting eight integrations (§1.5); a platform whose own security documentation places third-party integration behaviour outside its security programme (§1.8); a published threat model of this exact platform to evaluate against (§2.4.1); and a systematic review naming a Home Assistant proof-of-concept as future work (§2.4.3).

section: 5.4 Decision 1 — the platform
text: No comparable combination of scale, documented harm, platform-acknowledged gap and published evaluation baseline was found for any other platform during the Chapter 2 search.

section: 5.5 The relocation problem

section: 5.7.1 What the primitive has to deliver
text: **S4 deserves particular attention, because it is where this project differs from its closest prior work.** §2.4.2's gateway MUD architecture consolidates every plug-in's declaration into a single gateway-level profile, enforced by a firewall that sees one host — so the effective policy for any plug-in becomes the union of all of them, and attribution is impossible in principle rather than merely unimplemented.

text: **I3 and I4 are eliminated on cost, and the arithmetic is the argument.** §5.6.3 measured a marginal sandbox at 136 MB using ordinary processes, against a device with 4 GB.

section: 5.7.2 The candidates
text: Namespaces add essentially nothing to that: they are kernel bookkeeping, not a runtime. gVisor adds a user-space kernel process per sandbox and intercepts every system call — and a Python interpreter is syscall-heavy.

section: 6.3.3 A defect the measurement found, which is not what it was looking for
text: The helper layer wires itself during construction and so lands in the first row. `RestoreStateData` registers there, which is why **no state is ever dumped and every `RestoreEntity` in the sandbox silently restores nothing**.

section: 6.3.3 A defect the measurement found, which is not what it was looking for
text: In Home Assistant 2026.8.3 the helper is used by one helper module and **28 shipped components** — `mqtt`, `template`, `group`, `filter`, `utility_meter`, `history_stats` and `zwave_js` among them — so a callback written on the assumption that its peers already exist is a plausible way for the second row to matter too.

section: 7.4.4 Coverage — F3, F4, N3, and the honest table
text: - **F3 — every enforcement decision attributable to a manifest clause.** Verified by requiring each decision record to carry a clause pointer (`confine/manifest.py`), and by checking that a decision with no attributable clause is impossible rather than merely unobserved. - **F4 — the declaration presentable before installation.** Discharged in §6.7 by `confine/describe.py`, which renders four states and shows denials at the same weight as grants. §3.4 explicitly bounds F4 to *availability* of the information; user comprehension is a human-factors question excluded in §3.7 and is not evaluated here. - **N3 — a stated failure mode, not a silent one.** Behaviour on mediator unavailability is specified and tested. §6.4.1 supplies the case that makes this concrete: the supervisor must detect that it is in the wrong cgroup position at startup and refuse, because `mkdir` succeeds from the wrong position and everything looks right until placement silently fails.

text: **Run 2026-09-03**, `framework/confine/endtoend_egress.py`, `experiments/end_to_end/results/pi5_nordpool_egress.json`. §7.25 closed F2 with two purpose-built coordinators polling `example.com` and `example.net`, and stated its own limit in the same section:

section: 7.27.1 Why `nordpool`, and why the choice is forced rather than convenient
text: §7.17.1 measured the ceiling on any end-to-end arm: **26 of 37 integrations need an API key, token, password, username, host or email** before their own config flow can complete, and an unconfined baseline meets the identical wall.

section: 7.44.1 The design
text: Security audit standards take the other side and prefer stopping the audited activity to losing its record *(Common Criteria's FAU_STG.4 and NIST SP 800-53's AU-5; both still to be verified against their primary texts before citation)*.

section: 7.44.1 The design
text: Jiang et al. [29] describe the attack itself as a "super producer": one unprivileged process generating events fast enough to corrupt a centralised auditing framework or paralyse the system, which they trace to the absence of isolation between the processes the framework audits.

section: 7.44.1 The design

section: 7.44.1 The design

section: 7.44.1 The design

section: 8.4.2 Every correction has been to a sentence, never to a measurement

section: 8.4.2 Every correction has been to a sentence, never to a measurement
text: That is the honest ranking of the five mechanisms: a paired baseline stops misattribution, two instruments bound each other, a self-test freezes a surprising fact, recomputation checks a sentence against its source — **and running unmodified real code finds the things none of the four were looking for.** It is also the most expensive, which is why it happened last and why §8.7's future work is ordered the way it is.

section: 8.8 The single ask of the platform
text: Of the four residual High risks, one is not a property of confinement at all.

section: 8.8 The single ask of the platform
text: **R3 — Home Assistant issues no scoped credential.** There is no read-only variant and no per-domain variant of a long-lived access token, so the mediator must hold full authority in order to mediate at all, and compromise of the mediator is total compromise. §5.15.3 named this as the single change that would most improve any confinement scheme for this platform, and §7.11 records that this evaluation cannot assess it because it is upstream.

section: 8.8 The single ask of the platform
text: **What Chapter 7 adds is that the consequence is now measured rather than reasoned about.** §7.15.3 confirms the platform credential live in the mediator's process, reachable seven ways by the same supported API — `gc.get_objects()` — that §2.4.1 used against an integration.

section: 8.8 The single ask of the platform
text: The design moves that credential out of reach of every confined integration and it cannot make the credential smaller.

section: 8.8 The single ask of the platform

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: **The claim held.** Unmodified, pre-existing integrations were confined; the published attack that forced the architecture was reproduced and defeated against a live credential; the 2021 file-theft pattern that this ecosystem actually suffered succeeds unconfined and recovers nothing confined; and the import-level compatibility cost across 77 integrations on two corpora, measured against an unconfined baseline both times, is zero.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: On the hardware the requirements name, the mediator is 63× clear of realistic demand with durability paid for on every decision.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: **The last measurement taken was the one that mattered most, and it failed first.** Running a single real community integration confined against its own real API found that the platform's own HTTP helper could not be constructed inside the sandbox at all — so the egress design had been unusable for the population it was built to serve, for as long as it had existed, behind a suite of tests that all passed.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: **The claim is also smaller than it sounds, and the report says so in the same voice it says the rest.** Compatibility is measured at import for 77 integrations and end-to-end for five, because 26 of 37 need a credential no measurement of any confinement scheme can produce.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: Two of eighteen threats are partial, two are retained by decisions taken before the artifact existed, and one was never evaluated.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: Three of the closest published model's eleven threats have no counterpart in this register at all, where §4.14 accounted for one.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: **And the thing that made the project defensible is not in the artifact.** Six of eight pre-registered predictions were wrong, every one caught by a measurement and none revised afterwards.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: A paired baseline stopped three misattributions that a traceback would have got wrong, and every one of them would have charged the design *more* than it deserved — which is the direction an author's own attributions tend to err in the opposite way.

section: 8.9 What a reader should take from this
text: Across four chapters and two full read-throughs, **every correction has been to a sentence next to a measurement, and none to a measurement.** That asymmetry is the most transferable result here.
